items.title: WHY is it so HARD to have TWO Internet Connections?
items.description: Go to http://protonvpn.com/apalrd to get 30% off a Proton Unlimited plan today! Lots of people want a backup internet connection. Maybe because some providers are cheap but unreliable, but more likely because of the real risk of physical damage, and the fact that maintaining two connections for very rare interruptions can make great business sense. But, we are stuck with complex multi-WAN routers, and configuring failover and load balancing by abusing Network Address Translation. Is there a better way? Imagine a world where you can get a connection (+router) from two ISPs, plug them both in to your switch, and it all works magically. IPv6 should be able to do that, in theory, but there are just a few details missing. items.title: Using MULTICAST to stream live TV around my house
items.description: Click this link https://boot.dev/?promo=APALRD and use my code APALRD to get 25% off your first payment for boot.dev. Today I am taking a look at the weird world of multicast, where packets get delivered more than once, and we route using a backwards routing table. But, once you understand how it works, a whole world of content distribution possibilities open up to you! Inspired by an old video by @TallPaulTech , I'm using live TV distribution as an example of how multicast works, and how it can potentially be a massive upgrade to your network in oddly niche use cases. items.title: The transport protocol you've never heard of - SCTP
items.description: Long ago, the Transmission Control Program helped bring reliable, ordered communication to the early unreliable networks. But, modern network applications are rapidly jumping ship to UDP-based protocols. But if UDP is so unreliable, why wouldn't every application use TCP? Back in 2000, the SIGTRAN group tried to solve the problems with TCP with a new transport-layer protocol, the Stream Control Transmission Protocol, which is almost magical in what it provides to applications compared to UDP or TCP. But, why didn't it take off? Where is it today? Today I'm finally starting to put my AS Number to use, rolling out my Content Delivery Network! Currently it's actually not delivering anything useful, just some neat statistics, but it's helping me learn how CDNs work and share that with all of you. Data on my blog: https://www.apalrd.net/posts/2026/asn_cdn/ Also feel free to do the dns test yourself: https://www.apalrd.net/myip/ Buy my merch or support me on ko-fi: https://ko-fi.com/apalrd Feel free to chat about my upcoming projects on Discord! https://discord.gg/xJsaEukAr4 Follow me on Mastodon: https://hachyderm.io/@apalrd Timestamps: 00:00 - Introduction 02:32 - Loading My Website 08:20 - BGP Setup 17:05 - DNS Setup 24:32 - The Winners
